name: PWA World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: Crowned in a June 1992 tournament final between two 600-pound-class monsters and defended almost every week the recap's own record covers, changing hands four times before the promotion's own summer ended — and a fifth time, for good, when its last PWA-billed holder lost it to the FWF's own Doctor Death at the Clash of the Masters.

name: PWA United States Championship
epitaph: Awarded as the June tournament's own consolation prize and defended more often, and more cleanly, than either of the PWA's other two belts across the whole recorded summer.

name: PWA Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Won on the same June tournament card as the singles belts and defended through a summer of run-ins and DQ finishes, changing hands only once on camera — an upset by the Dogs of War — before it reached Crime & Punishment, its last PWA-billed holders, in time for the Clash of the Masters.
